newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Casino authority rejects Packer criticisms.
newsitem.headline: Casino authority rejects Packer criticisms.

text.p: The Casino Control Authority (CCA) of New South Wales said on Friday it rejected criticism from Kerry Packer's listed company that it was responsible for Packer's withdrawal from a deal involving the Sydney Harbour Casino.

Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd last Saturday cancelled a A$240 million deal to buy 85 percent of the management rights and a 10 percent stake in Sydney Harbour Casino Holdings Ltd from Las Vegas casino operator Showboat Inc.
The withdrawal fuelled speculation that Packer had instead decided to focus his merger activities on newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd in which he has 15 percent.

CCA chairman Christopher Cullen said the CCA had provided all necessary assistance to PBL and could not understand the criticisms made by PBL chairman Brian Powers, who said in Saturday's statement that the authority had not allowed Showboat to provide PBL with documentation to proceed with due diligence.
Powers also said the CCA had sought a payment of A$500,000 ahead of releasing the documentation.
Cullen said the payment was in fact related to probity investigations which PBL had requested and which PBL had said in mid-April that it was prepared to pay.
